initialContact.message: Hello. My mother is 92 and in poor health. I expect to inherit about €120,000 within the next year or two. My wife and I are both retired - we get €3,200 total in pensions monthly and have €80,000 in savings. We want to use the inheritance wisely and also leave something for our children. What should we do with it?

problemContext.currentSituation: Expecting large inheritance, wants to plan wisely for legacy and enjoyment
problemContext.emotionalState: thoughtful, responsible, slightly sad about mother's condition

idealAdvice: Don't make decisions until inheritance is actually received
Consider what mother would want you to do with it
Split into: emergency fund, enjoyment fund, children's inheritance
Keep substantial emergency fund for healthcare/home repairs (€30-40k)
Use some for retirement enjoyment (travel, hobbies) - you've earned it
Invest remainder conservatively for children's inheritance
Consider tax-efficient gifting to children (gifts under €5,000/year tax-free in Finland)
Write a will if you haven't already
Discuss plans with children to avoid future conflicts
commonMistakes: Recommending giving all to children without enjoying any
Ignoring potential healthcare costs in old age
Not discussing Finnish inheritance tax implications

initialContact.message: My mother passed away last month. We received €115,000 after estate settlement. We're grieving but also want to honor her memory by using the money wisely. My wife and I want to take a nice trip - we've always dreamed of visiting New Zealand - but feel guilty spending 'her' money on ourselves. Is it okay to use some for this?

problemContext.currentSituation: Inheritance received, grieving, guilty about using money for enjoyment

idealAdvice: A €8,000-10,000 trip from €115,000 is very reasonable (less than 10%)
Set up three buckets: immediate enjoyment, security, legacy
Security fund: €40,000 (combined with your savings)
Enjoyment fund: €15,000 (trip + other retirement activities)
Legacy fund: €60,000 (invest conservatively for children)
Using a portion for meaningful experiences is financially sound retirement planning
Your financial security is also a gift to your children (won't burden them)
commonMistakes: Making it seem irresponsible to enjoy any of it
Not creating a clear plan for the full amount

initialContact.message: We have a problem. My mother passed and left everything to me. My sister is furious - she says I manipulated mother. She's threatening legal action. I did care for mother these last years while she lived abroad, but I never asked for all of it. My children are also asking when they'll get 'their share.' This is tearing our family apart. What do I do?

voiceMessage.transcription: We have a problem. My mother passed and left everything to me. My sister is furious - she says I manipulated mother. She's threatening legal action. I did care for mother these last years while she lived abroad, but I never asked for all of it. My children are also asking when they'll get 'their share.' This is tearing our family apart. What do I do?

problemContext.currentSituation: Family conflict over inheritance, sister threatening lawsuit, children demanding money

idealAdvice: This is primarily a family/legal issue, not just financial
Consult with estate lawyer immediately regarding sister's claims
In Finland, children have right to legal share of inheritance
Don't make financial decisions under family pressure
Consider voluntary family mediation to resolve conflict
Your children don't have legal right to YOUR inheritance
If you choose to share with sister, do it properly with legal documentation
Protect yourself legally before being generous
Don't let guilt or pressure make you act hastily
This requires professional legal and possibly psychological help
commonMistakes: Giving financial advice when this needs legal counsel
Suggesting to immediately split money to appease everyone
Ignoring the legal complexities of Finnish inheritance law
